SMTO-EXE-0014 — The blocking job changed before your choice was saved

GUID: 34b43ba6-5bc5-4f52-b3f3-4c32083352f2
Slug: resource-reconciliation-stale-revision
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • While you were deciding what to do about a job that was blocking your task, that job's situation changed. SMTO didn't apply your choice, and your blocked command still hasn't started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment for the recovery card in the task (the one with the Wait until the job state changes button) to refresh, or reload the page. SMTO reloads the card after this message, and the new card shows what the blocking job is doing now.
  2. Read the updated card, then select Wait until the job state changes or Resolve forcefully by terminating job again. Your earlier choice was tied to the old situation, so it has to be made again for the current one.
  3. If the card is gone, check whether the task has carried on by itself. When the blocking job finishes on its own, there's nothing left to choose.

What success looks like

  • The card shows Job state updated, or the task continues with its next command.

If it still fails

  • If this keeps appearing, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't press the same button over and over; each press is checked against the latest state and will be refused while things keep changing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The resource reconciliation decision was rejected (409) because its decision ID, blocker revision, blocker identities or replayed action no longer matched the current saved blocker state.

What this means

  • Reconciliation compared the supplied decision/revision, blocker identity or replayed action with current saved evidence and found a mismatch. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Reconciliation compared the supplied decision/revision, blocker identity or replayed action with current saved evidence and found a mismatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare current blocker revision and decision identity with the submitted values, including any intervening control action.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the run's resource_reconciliation_request (decision_id, blocker_revision) and submit the action against that current projection; the UI reloads it after a 409. If it recurs, compare the Gateway job's resource_decisions and blocker identities with the run's prerequisites to see what keeps changing.
  • Refresh the current resource candidate and revision, then reconcile against that state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A refreshed decision uses the current revision and matching operation identities.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
